analogs.covers: How it lives and hunts: the solitary apex predator of the coast. It hauls out alone on a floe to doze for hours, patrols the water off its own stretch of shore, and waits for the young penguins' first swims. It takes fish, krill and the pups of other seals, and lunges from the water at the edge

How it holds ground: a shark that stays faithful to its home reef and patrols it daily. Before it attacks an intruder it performs one of the best-known threat displays in the sea: an arched back, raised snout and lowered fins, then a sudden strike

headline: A leopard seal on its own stretch of sea that guards it like a grey reef shark: the coastal Spinosaurus holds one piece of ocean and takes the young of the giants that swim through.

setting.label: One sea territory: island chain, sea cliffs, kelp shallows, shoal or deep ocean
setting.note: Claims exactly one bright-green sea area on the profile map: Palm Islands with Castaway Isle, Coastal Bluffs, Kelp Vale, Stonebed Shoal or the Abyssal Depths. It drinks outside the territory at fresh water it never defends: Rocky Lake, Dark Pond or the lake at Lakeside Meadow. Neutral gathering and courtship at Triad Falls, Wollemi Forest and Grand Falls.

playsLike: You are the Spinosaurus of the sea. You claim one sea territory, for example Palm Islands, the Coastal Bluffs or Kelp Vale, and you roam only inside it, like a leopard seal off its own piece of shore or a grey reef shark on its home reef. Everything in your water is your business. You shadow intruders along the waterline, display your sail and give three aggressive calls, and after 10 seconds you lunge, the Spinosaurus version of the reef shark's hunched threat display. Inside your territory you may start any hunt up to Apex. Your real speciality is the young of the sea giants: Leedsichthys calves on their migration and young Tylosaurus, because an adult Tylosaurus outswims you (900 to 750). You doze on a beach or a rock with your sail turned to the sun, as a leopard seal lies on its floe, and you dip often so your skin doesn't crack. Salt water doesn't quench your thirst, so you swim out regularly to fresh water beyond your borders, drink peacefully and come straight back. You never defend that water.

why.text: "Within a lifetime, Spinosaurus will exist both in fresh water and salt water." Some end up "preferring a lazy lifestyle touring saltwater areas, while most possessively claim territory in freshwater lakes and rivers." The profile map backs this with bright-green claimable sea areas: Kelp Vale, Coastal Bluffs, Abyssal Depths, Palm Islands and Stonebed Shoal.

"To begin this defense, Spinosaurus FIRST display their sail and issue x3 aggressive calls". After 10 seconds it lunges. A grey reef shark defends its reef the same way: a showy threat display first, then a sudden attack.

Spinosaurus "prefer to hunt their offspring" when they take on Tylosaurus and "enjoy hunting Leedsichthys offspring". A leopard seal patrols below the penguin colony for exactly that: the young on their first swims.
"When hunting, Spinosaurus become alarmingly passive and silent in water." The display is only for defence. A hunting leopard seal gives no warning either.

"All Spinosaurus bask frequently, aiming to direct their large sails directly in line of the sun's rays." This is the leopard seal's long doze on the floe, on the beaches of Palm Islands or the rocks of the Coastal Bluffs.

"Spinosaurus can be fickle over their water source, and move on to new territories when resources are low." It holds one territory at a time. When the fish run out, it leaves for a new one instead of holding two.
Apex tier, 6,000 combat weight, 1,100 HP. Water cruise 500 and sprint 750 for 167 s: level with Leedsichthys (750), slower than adult Tylosaurus (900 for 222 s).

notLike: Leopard seals and reef sharks never need fresh water. You do, and your drinking spot lies outside your territory, so you use it peacefully and never defend it.
A grey reef shark often rests in loose groups by day. Outside a pairbond you are a loner, and every other Spinosaurus in your water is a rival.
Neither animal forms pairbonds, while Spinosaurus yearn for one partner for life.
twist: The contrast with your freshwater cousin: the grizzly guards a river, you guard a piece of the sea. You are still one species and court together at Triad Falls.
